Attacks of Opportunity are now EXTREMELY RARE, due to how specific they are and the lost triggers.

Attacks made with your reaction (like from the Mage Slayer or Sentinel feats) are NOT attacks of opportunity. By default, you cannot attack someone because they are using a ranged attack (like a spell or a bow). Instead, it's ruled that the nearby enemy is "distracting" them and they get disadvantage on their roll.

You can houserule anything you want, but judging by the fact that you don't get an attack of opportunity from someone using a bow next to you, sheathing a weapon probably wouldn't either.

On top of that, proficiency probably should be the restriction here, not Martial vs. Simple. Sure, Simple weapons might be easier to stow, but that's probably also part of the reason why almost everyone is proficient in them. They're easier to use in every way. To me, if you're proficient in a Martial weapon then you feel as if the Martial weapon is just as easy as a Simple one, stowing included.

As of right now, proficiency doesn't matter TOO much when it comes to weapons or skills, especially at early levels. It's most important for armor (disadvantage on everything you do without it). I'd tack on a penalty of provoking attacks of opportunity whenever you use an action or skill you are not proficient with.
